Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has called on the state’s political class to put aside past disagreements and work together for the development of the state as he was sworn in for a second term. Adeleke made the call on Friday while addressing dignitaries and residents at the Osogbo Township Stadium, where he took the oath of office. He said unity among citizens, irrespective of political affiliations, was essential to the state’s collective progress. “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he said. The governor commended the people of the state for their resilience and commitment to protecting democracy, describing their support as a model for the country. Their commitment to democracy is today a national model,” he said. Outlining his priorities for the new term, Adeleke said his administration would focus on citizens’ welfare, infrastructure development, industrialisation, agriculture, the digital economy, tourism, wealth creation and the development of women and young people. He said his government would immediately establish the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission to improve electricity supply and support economic growth. He noted, “As growth depends on steady power supply, we will immediately set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission. This is in line with the power sector law I signed earlier this year. We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” On the lingering local government crisis in the state, Adeleke said President Bola Tinubu had intervened and expressed optimism that the dispute would be resolved within a week. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter. In the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he added. The deputy governor, Kola Adewusi, was sworn in at 11:24am, while Adeleke took his oath at 11:34am. The oaths were administered by the Chief Judge of Osun State, Justice Oyebola Adepele-Ojo. Vice-President Kashim Shettima led dignitaries from across the political, traditional and business sectors to the ceremony. Among those present were APC National Leader, Chief Bisi Akande; Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa; former APC National Secretary, Senator Iyiola Omisore; PDP National Treasurer, Prince Diran Odeyemi; and former Labour Party presidential candidate, Datti Baba-Ahmed. Traditional rulers at the event included the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi; the Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Akeem Owoade; the Olubadan of Ibadan, Oba Rashidi Ladoja; the Soun of Ogbomoso, Oba Ghandi Olaoye; and the Ataoja of Osogbo, Oba Jimoh Olanipekun. Adeleke’s elder brother, Dr Deji Adeleke, led members of the Adeleke family and business leaders to the inauguration. They included Afrobeat star David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido; Modupe Adeleke-Sanni; Tunji Adeleke; Shina Adeleke, also known as Shina Rambo; and Adebayo Adeleke, popularly known as B-Red.
